classification: Conditional arithmetic and code-level constraints; not a causal attribution or measured per-request demand.

code_facts.finding: Count preflight obtains one RPM permit with zero tokens; inference then obtains one RPM permit weighted by verified_count + prepared max_output_tokens. The count HTTP and both waits share one300-second deadline.
Permits occupy a rolling60-second history; a request may use initially free capacity. Permits are not refunded after failure or cancellation. These permits are not money.
Absent max_output_tokens defaults to4096; an explicit smaller positive limit is retained, and larger requests are clipped to4096. The run aggregates do not prove every completion used4096.

A verified completion requires reported usage_input >= counted_input, not equality; actual_output <= output_limit is also checked. Completed usage_input totals cannot be equated to exact-count permit totals.

assumptions: For each of the963 verified completions, exact counted_input equals the reported usage_input.
For each of those completions, prepared max_output_tokens is4096.
Only completed-response inference permits are counted; failed/uncertain attempts, count RPM permits, service time and waits are excluded.
conditional_scenario.comparison_to_coding_window: 29.65945 token-capacity-minutes is close to a30-minute coding window under these assumptions. It is not a measured wait duration, minimum elapsed time, or proof the limiter caused the original outcomes.
conditional_scenario.code_level_bound: Because counted_input <= verified usage_input and output_limit <=4096,23727563 is an upper bound on aggregate inference permit weights for these completed responses under the frozen code; it is not an observed lower bound or a requirement demonstrated by the receipts. Failed or uncertain attempts can consume additional permits.

useful_implications.statement: Increasing active workers to100 does not increase the shared800kTPM ceiling. Repeated large request contexts and conservative maximum-output reservations can compete with a bounded coding window.

useful_implications.status: hypothesis for a controlled future experiment
useful_implications.statement: Bound exact per-task authority/context and record per-request permit weight, wait and service durations before changing concurrency or deadlines. The existing documentation-read output totals are bytes and command heuristics, not measured input-count contributions.

unmeasured_or_unproven: Per-request exact counted_input, prepared max_output_tokens and actual granted inference permit weights were not retained as an auditable final aggregate.
Per-request queue-entry, count permit, count HTTP start/end, inference permit, upstream send, first response and settlement times are needed to reconstruct pressure, bursts and deadline losses.
Initially available capacity, rolling-window shape, request ordering, cancellations, failed/uncertain attempts and model/service latency prevent converting the quotient to observed wall time.

At least one local queue expiry is observed in the existing safe activity allowlist; repeated sticky snapshots are not distinct expiries, and94 failed/uncertain outcomes are not94 proven upstream429s.

No evidence here establishes pacing as the cause of0 original validated workers, input-count equality, all output limits being4096, an AFK advantage, actual provider cost or actual provider quota sufficiency.

instrument_only_proposal: Retain allowlisted numeric permit weights and monotonic phase timestamps without prompts, task tokens, headers or content.
Use an already approved future controlled comparison to vary bounded prompt context/output reservation or deadline one factor at a time; keep all original failures and full delivery clock.

benchmark.scope: Offline code reading and arithmetic; no runtime mutation or simulation of an observed trace.
